messages:
mira: Heads up — since ~02:00 UTC we started seeing edge prober timeouts to AAAA records in a few regions. ALB healthchecks marked some backends OOS. :grimacing:
jon: saw it on-alert too, looks like the prober is preferring AAAA and failing over NAT64 paths. Any logs?
mira: prober logs show repeated connect errors after DNS returns AAAA and A. snippet: 
```
2026-03-18T02:05:12Z prober[1]: resolving service.internal -> AAAA 2606:4700:... -> connect: EHOSTUNREACH
2026-03-18T02:05:12Z prober[1]: fallback to A + retry -> OK (but slow)
```
paul: we rolled an eBPF policy change in canary last night that tweaks iptables conntrack handling for host-networked flows. could be interfering with NAT64/ICMPv6.
jon: can you confirm whether the failing nodes have the well-known NAT64 prefix (64:ff9b::/96) injected?
mira: checked a failing node, `ip -6 route` shows no NAT64 prefix. trying `curl -6 -v http://64:ff9b::1` times out.
paul: hm. eBPF policy might be dropping RA/RS or ICMPv6 types required for ND. If ND fails you won't learn the right neighbor entries for the tunnel to NAT64 gateway.
infra-bot: deploy 1769.4 -> west-2 completed at 01:50 UTC (canary 5 hosts).
mira: quick experiment: toggled `sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1` on a bad node and NAT64 reachability briefly returned, then stopped after ~30s. looks like something repeatedly overwrote routes.
jon: can you dump `bpftool map` and `bpftool prog` from the host and attach? also `ip -6 neigh` and `ip route show table all`.
mira: attaching small logs inline: 
``
BPFTABLE: map_id 23 name conntrack_v6 entries 0/8192
PROG: xdp_drop id 45 pinned /sys/fs/bpf/host/xdp_drop
IPNEIGH: no entries for 64:ff9b::/96
```
liz: note: ALB healthchecks are configured as dualstack. our prober resolves both A and AAAA; if resolver prefers AAAA the prober will try v6 path first which triggers the issue.
paul: canary rollback ready (PR #483) but want to be sure it's the root cause. for immediate mitigation we can force prober to prefer IPv4 for healthchecks (`prefer_ipv4: true`) or make healthcheck resolver query A only.
jon: agree. also add an alert when `ip -6 route` doesn't contain the NAT64 prefix for >1m on edge nodes.
mira: rolling the prober config change to canary now (prefer_ipv4 = true) — will monitor.
paul: created a short-term host rule to allow ICMPv6 type 133/134 (RS/RA) through the eBPF filter in canary.
jon: plan for long-term: fix eBPF policy to preserve ICMPv6 ND and ensure our startup path injects the NAT64 prefix if node is in v4-only zone. file a ticket for test coverage.
mira: opened INF-2456 with timeline, logs, and rollback plan; assigning to @paul and @jon. :white_check_mark:
jon: watching the canary now. if failures drop to <0.2% we can continue rollout. ping me if rate spikes.
paul: will follow up with a postmortem draft after we stabilize.
mira: thanks, team. monitoring dashboards look better after the prober change — will update once canary finishes. :eyes:
